chapter: Looking back: rock, blues, childhood and guitar innovators
title: Ukulele and banjo, then Selma and his mother's dance band
summary: He was half-famous on ukulele, took up banjo to play in his mother's band, and they moved to Selma where she taught at Paine and led a dance band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: First the banjo, then the guitar.
Oh, I didn't know about that.
Sure, I told you that my mother gave my sister this ukulele and I just took it and played it, and instant fame.

Well, around Montgomery and my mother taught music also in a school there, in Selma, Alabama, you know. So I could play, you know, and everybody knew that I could play, and so I was kind of half -- let's say half famous, you know.
Oh, yes, and then I took up the banjo. And did very well with that.
Oh, for quite a while, but I wanted to play in my mother's band so I got this banjo. See, she had a little band and so I got the banjo and --

Yeah. And we went to Selma, moved to Selma because she got this teaching job in this school here. It was a little school, Paine University. And she went there and then she got married there, and she got a band. So she quit teaching school when she got married, and the only thing she did was just play dances and we would travel all around the state, you know. And I was part of the band, you know. And after that as I told you I took up the guitar. But I always was drawn to strings. You know. Never -- I was never a reed man.
